title_zh: 别再拿“傻钱”：Craig Schedler（Intuit Ventures）谈企业风投的直投与 LP 双轮
subtitle_zh: Intuit Ventures 负责人 Craig Schedler 分享企业风投如何用 LP 出资、尽调基金与“翻译”内外需求创造价值。

turns.en: Every holiday season, I put pressure on myself to find the perfect gift, but getting it right isn't always easy. That's why Sephora is my go-to for holiday gifting.
turns.zh: 每到节日季，我都会给自己施压，想挑到完美的礼物，但要选对可不容易。所以节日送礼，我首选 Sephora。

turns.en: Even if you're not a beauty shopper, Sephora has gifts for everyone, and their beauty advisors can help take the guesswork out of gifting. This holiday season, we all Sephora. Whether they're into fragrance, makeup, skin care, or hair care, Sephora makes it easy to find something thoughtful they'll actually love.
turns.zh: 就算你平时不买美妆产品，Sephora 也有适合每个人的礼物，他们的美妆顾问还能帮你省去送礼靠猜的烦恼。这个节日季，我们都选 Sephora。无论对方喜欢香水、彩妆、护肤还是护发，Sephora 都能让你轻松挑到一份贴心、他们真正会喜欢的礼物。

turns.en: Shop gifts at Sephora and give something beautiful. Your Sausage McMuffin with Egg didn't change. Your receipt did. The Sausage McMuffin with Egg Extra Value meal includes a hash brown and a small coffee for just $5. Only at McDonald's for a limited time.
turns.zh: 到 Sephora 挑礼物，送出一份美好。你的猪柳蛋麦满分（Sausage McMuffin with Egg）没变，变的是你的账单。猪柳蛋麦满分超值套餐包含一份薯饼和一杯小杯咖啡，只要 5 美元。仅限 McDonald's，限时供应。

turns.en: Price and participation may vary. Promotion pricing may be lower than meal pricing. Welcome to Swimming with Allocators, the VC podcast from the LP perspective.
turns.zh: 价格和参与门店可能有所不同。促销价可能低于套餐价。欢迎收听 Swimming with Allocators，一档从 LP（有限合伙人）视角出发的风投播客。

turns.en: With your host, Alexa Binz and Ernest Sepp. You ready? Let's dive in. Thank you so much for being here, Craig. Thank you for having me. It's great to be here today.
turns.zh: 本期主持是 Alexa Binz 和 Ernest Sepp。准备好了吗？我们开始吧。非常感谢你来做客，Craig。谢谢你们邀请我，今天很高兴能来。

turns.en: Absolutely. Before we get into everything that Into Adventures does, we'd love to learn a little bit about you and your journey leading Northwestern Mutual Ventures program and things that led up to you being at Into It.
turns.zh: 当然。在我们聊 Intuit Ventures 做的这些事情之前，我们想先了解一下你本人，以及你一路带领 Northwestern Mutual Ventures 项目、最终来到 Intuit 的经历。

turns.en: Yeah. I spent the first part of my career in investment banking and had the opportunity to work with a lot of founder-led businesses. That sort of piqued my curiosity around venture and what founders do and being able to support them and work with them.
turns.zh: 好的。我职业生涯的前半段是在投资银行度过的，有机会跟很多创始人主导的企业打交道。这就勾起了我对风投的好奇——创始人都在做什么，以及怎么去支持他们、和他们共事。

turns.en: And so I had the opportunity to join Northwestern Mutual back in 2014. Really at this, the inception of what became FinTech. It was just becoming a word.
turns.zh: 所以我在 2014 年有机会加入了 Northwestern Mutual，正好是后来所谓金融科技（FinTech）的萌芽期。当时这个词才刚开始流行起来。

turns.en: It was the very, very early days of what I'll call FinTech 1.0. So if you think back, it was all the disruption of consumer FinTech. It was disintermediating banks and insurance companies and incumbent wealth managers.
turns.zh: 那是我所称的 FinTech 1.0 的最最早期。回想一下，那时候全都是面向消费者的金融科技的颠覆——它在对银行、保险公司和老牌财富管理机构做去中介化（disintermediation）。

turns.en: And so it was this fascinating time for Northwestern Mutual to think about what does the future hold for us? And so it was tasked with standing up Northwestern Mutual Future Ventures, which was our corporate venture program, helping Northwestern Mutual prepare for that future that was at the time uncertain and what was going to happen and what their role was for it. And so I spent about 12 years building and running the team there.
turns.zh: 所以对 Northwestern Mutual 来说，那是个很有意思的时期，要去思考未来会带给我们什么。于是我受命组建了 Northwestern Mutual Future Ventures，也就是我们的企业风投（corporate venture）项目，帮助 Northwestern Mutual 为当时还不确定的未来做准备——未来会发生什么、他们在其中扮演什么角色。我在那里花了大约 12 年来搭建并运营这个团队。

turns.en: Invested in a lot of early successful kind of FinTech 1.0 companies. We were early investors in Betterment and in Chime and some very successful companies that delivered great financial results and performance, as well as strong strategic values.
turns.zh: 我们投了很多早期成功的 FinTech 1.0 公司。我们是 Betterment 和 Chime 的早期投资人，还有一些非常成功的公司，它们既带来了出色的财务回报和业绩，也带来了很强的战略价值。

turns.en: We built the program over the years. So from that seat saw how FinTech evolved, how InsureTech came into being, and more recently, WealthTech was the area that we were focused on pretty heavily. And so from that experience, had the opportunity to join into it.
turns.zh: 这些年我们把这个项目一点点做起来。所以坐在那个位置上，我见证了金融科技（FinTech）如何演进、保险科技（InsureTech）如何兴起，而最近这几年，财富科技（WealthTech）是我们重点关注的领域。也正是凭借这段经历，我才有机会加入 Intuit。

turns.en: And I think it's been a fascinating time to join into it as we look at how the technology landscape continues to evolve with AI and how that pushes technology forward and forces incumbents to look at their businesses in a different way. But what really tracked me into it was the breadth of the platform and the reach of it. So a lot of ways in which we can drive value across the organization. And so joined into it about a year ago now and really focusing on how we can drive
turns.zh: 我觉得，加入 Intuit 正值一个很有意思的时期：我们看到技术格局如何随着 AI 不断演进，AI 如何推动技术向前，并迫使老牌企业用不同的眼光重新审视自己的业务。而真正吸引我加入 Intuit 的，是这个平台的广度和触达范围——我们能在整个组织的很多层面创造价值。所以我大约一年前加入了 Intuit，真正专注于我们如何能够推动

turns.en: into it, drive insights and new opportunities for partnerships into into its businesses. So around our consumer businesses, so TurboTax and Credit Karma, looking at the future of consumer finance, and then also around our SMB product, our small business, you know, QuickBooks, obviously there, and then also our emerging mid-market business. So looking at our into an enterprise sweet and how we help mid-market businesses grow and succeed. So like I said, it's really just a
turns.zh: Intuit 把洞察和新的合作机会带进它各项业务里。比如围绕我们的消费者业务——TurboTax 和 Credit Karma——去看消费者金融的未来；还有围绕我们的小微企业（SMB）产品，也就是小企业，显然 QuickBooks 就在那里；再就是我们新兴的中端市场（mid-market）业务。所以是去看 Intuit Enterprise Suite，以及我们如何帮助中端市场企业成长和成功。就像我说的，这真的是一个

turns.en: it's a fascinating platform and a great time to be into it. Craig, during our prep conversation, I was really intrigued by your experience at Northwestern Mutual and kind of being at the ground floor of building that out.
turns.zh: 非常迷人的平台，而现在正是待在 Intuit 的好时候。Craig，在我们录制前的沟通里，我对你在 Northwestern Mutual 的经历、以及你算是从零开始搭建那个项目的过程特别感兴趣。

turns.en: And I'm curious now that you're into it, what were some of the lessons you learned with developing, you know, a corporate venture program? It can look a lot of different ways that you've applied to into it. I think, you know, I've been through enough of this in, you know, a decade plus of being in corporate venture. I think the number one thing I've learned is you need to be very clear on your North Star. What does the organization need and want and value
turns.zh: 我很好奇，如今你在 Intuit，你在搭建企业风投项目这件事上学到了哪些经验？它可以呈现出很多不同的形态，而你把哪些用到了 Intuit 上？——我觉得，我在企业风投这行干了十多年，经历得够多了。我认为我学到的头号经验就是：你必须非常清楚自己的北极星（North Star）是什么。组织需要一个企业风投项目做什么、想要什么、看重什么？

turns.en: from a corporate venture program? And I don't think there's a right or wrong answer to that necessarily. I think there's variations of good and maybe not quite as good, but I think overall like every company is going to approach it differently, have different expectations and have different aspects of the program that they want to derive value from. So it can start with, you know, an M&A pipeline, you know, if you're simply looking for companies to get a toehold
turns.zh: ——从这个项目里得到什么？我觉得这不一定有对错之分。有的是好，有的可能没那么好，但总体而言，每家公司都会用不同的方式去做，有不同的预期，也有各自想从这个项目里获取价值的不同侧面。所以它可以从一条并购（M&A）管线开始——如果你只是想找一些公司先占个落脚点（toehold），

turns.en: in to understand and ultimately look to acquire those businesses, that's one way that that can be effective. I think one other way can be more financially driven if you're thinking about it strictly from a financial perspective, although within a corporate setting I think that can be a little bit of a challenge. But then I think that's like everything in between. I think what I've seen be successful is how can you really drive strategic insights? You know, I think the
turns.zh: 去理解它们、并最终考虑收购这些业务，那是一种可行的方式。我觉得另一种方式可以更偏财务驱动——如果你纯粹从财务角度来考虑的话，尽管在企业内部这么做我觉得会有点挑战。然后中间还有各种形态。我见过真正成功的，是你能否真正带来战略洞察。我觉得，

turns.en: business units and the GMs and, you know, the leaders of businesses across Intuit are spending a lot of their time focused on, you know, what their business is doing, what they're trying to build, what they're trying to deliver in the next quarter, the next year, the next couple of years even. And I view our role as supporting them and enhancing their knowledge with outside perspective.
turns.zh: Intuit 内部各个业务单元、总经理（GM）和业务负责人，把大量时间都放在自己的业务上——他们在做什么、想打造什么、下个季度、下一年、甚至未来几年要交付什么。而我把我们的角色定位为：用外部视角去支持他们、拓展他们的认知。

turns.en: So how do we go about investing in companies that can deliver that value, that insight into our business? And so we can go about that a variety of ways, but really sort of coming back to when we meet a company, we say, hey, okay, that's something that's interesting to this part of our business, or we know this is on our strategic roadmap for next year. We need to help the business understand like, here's an approach and here's something that could be a potential
turns.zh: 那么，我们怎么去投资那些能为业务带来这种价值、这种洞察的公司呢？做法可以有很多种，但归根结底，当我们遇到一家公司时，我们会说：嘿，好，这个东西对我们业务的这一块很有意思，或者我们知道它就在我们明年的战略路线图上。我们需要帮助业务去理解：这是一种思路，这是一个潜在的

turns.en: partner. It could be some way that, you know, Intuit could potentially work with a company as part of a go-to-market strategy. You're overseeing both direct investments as well as some LP commits. And you've said you're surprised that more corporate venture programs don't also take this LP route. Yes, it's interesting to me. I think, again, a lot of corporate venture funds approach things differently. And I think primarily where they start is around direct investments. It's
turns.zh: 合作伙伴，也可能是 Intuit 能以某种方式与一家公司合作、作为市场进入（go-to-market）战略的一部分。——你既负责直接投资，也做一些 LP 出资（LP commits）。你说过，让你意外的是，更多的企业风投项目并没有走 LP 这条路。——是的，这一点我觉得很有意思。我觉得，很多的企业风投基金做事方式各不相同。而我认为它们主要的起点大多是直接投资。这

turns.en: sort of the most obvious route. There are startups, we're a company, we can allocate capital, we can invest in these companies, we can gather whatever value or we can, you know, partner with them in whatever way is important. So I think that's sort of where most corporate venture programs start.
turns.zh: 算是最显而易见的路径：那里有初创公司，我们是一家企业，我们可以配置资本、可以投资这些公司、可以获取各种价值，或者以任何重要的方式与它们合作。所以我觉得，这就是大多数企业风投项目的起点。

turns.en: I think the piece that does get missed is the LP element. And virtually every corporate venture fund that I know is, you know, they've got limited resources. They're resource constrained.
turns.zh: 我觉得真正被忽略的那一块，是 LP 这个环节。而且几乎我认识的每一支企业风投基金，都是——他们资源有限，受到资源约束。

turns.en: And in addition to doing sort of the venture aspect of it, there's the internal stakeholder management piece of it. And so I think corporate team, some corporate venture teams sometimes miss that. You can supplement and compliment what you're doing with direct investments with a thoughtful, well-structured LP program. And I think that gets overlooked for a few reasons. One is you sort of understand startups maybe, but then there's this other world of
turns.zh: 而且除了做风投这部分，还有内部利益相关方管理这一块。所以我觉得，有些企业风投团队有时会忽略这一点：你可以用一个经过深思熟虑、结构良好的 LP 项目，来补充和增益你在直接投资上做的事。我认为这一点被忽视有几个原因。一是你也许大致懂初创公司，但另外还有那么一个充满

turns.en: terms and jargon and funds that you don't get. There's GPs. What is that? You know, what does it mean to be an LP? So I think there's sort of an additional education element that sometimes isn't there. So I think that's number one. I think the other thing is it can be looked at as kind of like outsourcing your role as, you know, I was given this responsibility to make investments and develop relationships with startups and the startup ecosystem, but then I'm going to go have
turns.zh: 术语、行话和基金的世界，是你搞不明白的。有 GP（普通合伙人），那是什么？做 LP 又意味着什么？所以我觉得这里还有一个额外的补课环节，而这个环节有时是缺失的。这是第一点。我觉得另一点是，它可能被看作是在把你的职责外包出去——就好像说，我拿到了这份职责，要去做投资、要和初创公司及初创生态建立关系，但接下来我却要去找

turns.en: someone could be perceived as do it for me. And I think that's a very narrow way of looking at it as saying, you know, I'm just going to have someone do it for me. So it can be very complimentary.
turns.zh: 别人，可能会被理解成让别人替我做。我觉得这是一种非常狭隘的看法，等于在说我就是找个人替我做。其实它可以是非常互补的。

turns.en: And I think it does surprise me sometimes that more corporate venture teams don't use LP commitments as part of kind of a broader strategy to deliver on the strategic objectives.
turns.zh: 所以我有时确实感到意外：更多的企业风投团队没有把 LP 出资作为更广泛战略的一部分，用来实现那些战略目标。

turns.en: How would you advise an organization to start that process? You know, I've, we've had on the show before, you know, Deloitte, the Canada National Office, Deloitte Ventures, they started their approach of even getting to understand the marketplace by investing in firms. But let's say you've already done kind of, as you said, the first start with directs. Now, how do you incorporate this other toolkit, tool in the toolkit box of investing in funds? What's the
turns.zh: 你会建议一个组织怎么开始这个过程呢？我们节目之前请过 Deloitte，就是 Deloitte 加拿大全国办公室、Deloitte Ventures，他们甚至是通过投资一些事务所来着手了解市场的。但假设你已经像你说的那样，先从直接投资起步了。那么，你要怎么把投资基金这个工具也纳入你的工具箱呢？什么是

turns.en: right way and right approach? Yeah, I think it really starts with, you know, if you are starting from a direct investment first or a direct investment exclusive approach, as you are out making those investments, you're inevitably going to meet venture funds, like you're going to run into other funds, obviously, that are looking at the same types of deals, the same opportunities, the same broad category of companies. And so I think you can develop an appreciation for who
turns.zh: 正确的方式和正确的路径？——是的，我觉得这真的要从这里说起：如果你是从直接投资优先、或者纯直接投资的方式起步，那么在你四处做这些投资的过程中，你不可避免地会遇到风投基金——你显然会碰到其他基金，它们在看同类型的项目、同样的机会、同一大类的公司。所以我觉得，你逐渐就能判断出谁

turns.en: you think is a good investor and who's maybe not quite as good or someone that's a little more focused on what you, the types of investments that you're interested in. So I think that can happen very naturally through, you know, just sort of being in the venture ecosystem, you can say, hey, you know, we've now run across this fund, the last four opportunities we've looked at, they've also been investing in or looking at. And so you sort of see like, we're quickly
turns.zh: 是好的投资人，谁可能没那么强，或者谁在你感兴趣的那类投资上更专注。所以我觉得，这可以非常自然地发生——只要你身处风投生态之中，你就能说：嘿，我们最近碰上了这支基金，我们看的最近四个项目，他们也在投或者也在看。于是你就发现，我们很快

turns.en: developing a, there's pattern here that, you know, we're seeing and looking at the same opportunities. And so I think that's one way. I think the other way is just you do, you know, through a little bit of cold outreach, if you were just interested in getting to no funds, again, that you had seen or met or seen in other settings, I think that's a really good way to to do that. And, you know, I think very astute GPs will quickly recognize that, you know, we're
turns.zh: 就形成了一个规律——我们在看同样的机会。所以这是一种方式。另一种方式是，你可以做一点点主动陌生联络（cold outreach），如果你只是想认识一些你见过、碰过、或在其他场合看到过的基金，我觉得这是很好的方式。而且我觉得，非常精明的 GP 会很快意识到，我们

turns.en: seeing this and, you know, could they be a potential LP for the next fund kind of thing. But I think that's a really great way is just through the direct investment program, you're going to start running into or, you know, engaging with and interacting with other funds.
turns.zh: 在看这些项目，进而想到他们会不会是我下一支基金的潜在 LP 之类的。但我认为，通过直接投资项目，你真的会开始碰到、并开始与其他基金接触和互动，这是非常好的方式。

turns.en: And that's a really great way to sort of see how they think, how they invest, what types of investments are, you know, our core to their focus and thesis. It's one thing to assume, you know, you bump into people, then they're part of kind of like, okay, this is a nexus of people that we could potentially invest in. But when it comes to the actual diligently funds, you're already, you know, as an organization building out a new practice and skill set of investing in
turns.zh: 而这也是很好的方式，去了解他们怎么思考、怎么投资，哪些类型的投资是他们关注和投资主题（thesis）的核心。碰上一些人是一回事——好，这些算是我们潜在可投的人脉节点。但真正要对基金做尽职调查（diligence）时又是另一回事——你作为一个组织，本来就已经在搭建投资初创公司这套全新的做法和技能，

turns.en: startups. How do you think about developing diligently funds as well? Like, especially given, as you mentioned earlier, each corporate venture program has a specific different north star or should have a north star. So how do you align that with the diligence of a fund? It's a very different approach to direct investment. I think what becomes important, what you focus on, how you approach diligence is different from a direct investment, I think for a whole host of
turns.zh: 那么你又怎么去培养对基金做尽调的能力呢？尤其是像你前面提到的，每个企业风投项目都有一个各自不同、或者说应该有一个北极星目标。那么你怎么把这个目标和对基金的尽调结合起来？——这与直接投资是很不一样的做法。我觉得，什么是重要的、你关注什么、你怎么做尽调，都跟直接投资不同，原因是有一大堆

turns.en: reasons. And I think from the GP's perspective, they need to understand that the diligence a corporate or potential corporate LP is going to want to do is probably going to look different from what I'll call traditional institutional LP. But I think when a corporate starts to evaluate a first fund, I think there's a few important things to look at. Number one is does their investment thesis align to areas we care about? Number one, obviously, like this needs to be
turns.zh: 原因。而且我觉得，站在 GP 的角度，他们需要明白：一家企业、或潜在的企业 LP 想要做的尽调，很可能跟我所说的传统机构 LP 不一样。但我认为，当一家企业开始评估一支基金时，有几件重要的事要看。第一，他们的投资主题是否与我们关注的领域一致？第一条很显然——这必须是一支

turns.en: a fund that is investing in areas that we're interested in. I think similarly, you can't expect any fund to invest in 100% of things that you care about. Like, a fund is going to have a mandate. Let's just say you can see they're investing in fintech, right? That's a pretty broad category. And if I'm an insurance company, I can't expect every investment they do to align perfectly to insurance or to wealth management or whatever. Like, they're building a portfolio,
turns.zh: 投资于我们感兴趣领域的基金。同样地，你不能指望任何一支基金 100% 都投在你关心的东西上。因为一支基金会有它的投资使命（mandate）。就说你能看出他们在投金融科技（fintech），对吧？那是个相当宽泛的类别。如果我是一家保险公司，我不能指望他们的每一笔投资都完美契合保险、或财富管理之类的。他们在构建一个投资组合，

turns.en: they're trying to select the best companies that they believe have potential for outsized returns. And so not every investment is going to fit perfectly. So I think you need to be realistic on how much of the portfolio, how much of the focus is going to align to your specific areas of interest. turns.zh: 作为 LP 想要的、以及便于 GP 管理自己工作量的那种合适的节奏。我不觉得要求一个投资委员会席位、或投资优先拒绝权（right of refusal）、或那些会改变基金投资方式的东西是合理的。我觉得要现实地看待：你能对 GP 有什么预期，反过来 GP 又能有什么预期。但我觉得，另外一件

turns.zh: 他们在外面募资时。所以要看什么是现实的、他们以前又做过什么。要一份他们寄给 LP 的材料看看——是不是就是一封简单的两页信，讲讲财务业绩就完了？这也是一种做法，如果这对他们的 LP 管用，那很好。但话说回来，这还是要落到你作为企业 LP 身上：你在找什么，并且理解什么是可能的、什么是现实的，然后就双方是否是潜在的合适对象，进行那种非常

turns.zh: 但接下来的问题是：AI 如何让这东西比老牌解决方案、甚至比那些已经存在一段时间的初创公司更好？比如说，一家 AI 原生的 A 轮（Series A）公司，跟一个更成熟的东西相比，不同在哪里？所以我觉得，我们看到的最大机会，显然就是围绕面向金融服务的垂直 AI，然后再把它拆解成一大堆

turns.zh: 金融服务内部的子垂直领域。——我觉得，作为 LP、作为企业 LP 拥有这些关系，其中一个好处就是：能把外面世界——坦白说尤其是你自己行业里——正在发生的所有变化，怎么去应对，反馈给母舰（mothership）的其余部分。你有没有什么轶事或故事，讲讲这类关系、或者某些在你常规项目源渠道之外的东西，你是怎么从

turns.zh: 或者，也许那对你们来说都太早了，但你们觉得那是个特别棒的创始人，你们会保持联系——能不能帮我们引荐一下？所以，抱着这个想法，我们最近为这里的一个领导团队做了一场关于代理式商务的分享会。我们自己已经见过几家，我们想用 GP 们所看到的东西来补充和增益，为我们的领导团队呈现一场很棒的分享会，

turns.zh: 但这确实很大程度上是一场翻译的游戏。当一家初创公司——不管是我们已经投过的、还是我们正在考虑投资的——想跟 Intuit 合作时，我们需要帮他们理解：会有一个流程、会有这些利益相关方，这不是一蹴而就的；每个大组织都有自己那套层级和机制来做这类事情。所以
